/-!
# Erdős Problem 645

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/645](https://www.erdosproblems.com/645)
- [BrLa99] Brown, Tom C. and Landman, Bruce M., Monochromatic arithmetic progressions with large
  differences. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1999), 21--35.
-/


namespace Erdos645

/--
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

This was first proved by Brown and Landman [BrLa99], who in fact show that this is always possible
with $d>f(x)$ for any increasing function $f$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos645.lean"]
theorem erdos_645 (c : ℕ → Bool) : ∃ x d, 0 < x ∧ x < d ∧
    (∃ C, c x = C ∧ c (x + d) = C ∧ c (x + 2 * d) = C) := by
  sorry

end Erdos645

reformulations.difference: Lean colours all natural numbers, including zero, but requires positive starting terms; Brown–Landman work with colourings of the positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since 0 < x < d, all three progression terms are positive. Restricting a colouring to the positive integers preserves every eligible progression, and every colouring of the positive integers extends arbitrarily to zero. The two universally quantified statements are therefore equivalent. This equivalence was proved without using the imported sorry theorem in /workspace/review/positive_equivalence.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/645 (including mathematical remarks and current status; HTML retrieved via https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/645)

Brown, T. C. and Landman, B. M., Monochromatic arithmetic progressions with large differences, Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 60 (1999), 21–35, especially §1 and Theorem 7: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S0004972700033293
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's affirmative claim: an arbitrary two-colouring has a monochromatic three-term progression with d > x. The shared existential Bool correctly expresses monochromaticity, and 0 < x < d excludes degenerate progressions. Lean boundary checks and small-colouring computations passed. Brown–Landman's Theorem 7 supports the stronger docstring remark; taking f(x)=x+1 gives the required strict bound. The source currently records PROVED (LEAN), agreeing with both metadata attributes. The linked proof states exactly the repository theorem. After two tactic-only compatibility edits in the sandbox, it compiled under the installed Lean version, with axioms only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
